lead_headline: Noble Steakhouse debuts in LoDo, Vaultaire opens subterranean HiFi bar at La Forêt, and Ash & Agave launches at Cherry Creek on day one of May's restaurant wave

restaurant.blurb: 8 opening leads, 1 closure lead today: Noble Steakhouse (LoDo), Vaultaire listening bar (Speer), Ariel's Cafe (Montbello), Vintage Himalayan (Rosedale reopening). Closure: The Pearl lesbian bar after one-year run.

liquor.blurb: Zero new applications today, maintaining the 7-day total at 2,386 licenses as the week-old database surge continues its washout. The massive count — up 14,813% from the prior week's 16 filings — represents a clear system event (mass renewals or batch processing) rather than legitimate new business activity. May 1st brings no individual applications of note, confirming the liquor license tracker has entered a post-flood quiet period with organic weekly volumes likely to normalize to historical 20-30 baselines once backend cleanup concludes.

reputation.blurb: Zero mentions yesterday drops the 7-day count to 40 across 14 sources — down 17% from last week's 48 and marking April's weakest daily showing in three weeks. Instagram (10) leads Wednesday's weekly tally ahead of Facebook (9), Reddit (6), and a three-way tie between Hoodline, Denver Post, and City Cast (3 each). Recent pickups include City Cast's LoDo nightlife ordinance coverage, Hoodline's Greenwood Village office seizure story, and social chatter about Temple Denver's evolution and scooter contract changes. The 40-mention pace lands 4% below April's 42-count monthly average, with Wednesday's zero suggesting end-of-month editorial slowdown ahead of May's reset.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +3 yesterday (3 new, 0 canceled) pushes MTD to +0 (+0.0/day) with 90-day net at +119. Wednesday's clean gain follows Tuesday's +1 crawl after Monday's −13 churn event that erased two weeks of momentum — the 7-day total now stands at −3 net (17 new, 20 canceled), down from last week's +16 and confirming April's final stretch has turned choppy. The past fortnight shows April 28th's 17-cancellation spike reversed 10 days of steady growth, leaving May's opening day with MTD flat at exactly zero net despite Wednesday's uptick. Current pace trails YTD's +1.3/day baseline by 100% as volatility replaces Q1's conversion stability, with May needing sustained daily gains to recover April's lost ground.
